sections.title: From compound to certification
sections.live: LIVE H2 → From Compound to Certification · six steps · step 03 says compression moulding; most flange gaskets are die-cut

fields.label: Steps
rows: Material compounding — polymer blending, additive integration and batch QC in our in-house lab. The cure system is set here — peroxide-cured EPDM where the joint sees steam or hot water, sulphur-cured where it does not.
Tool or die design — moulds for shaped gaskets, cutting dies for flat ones, made in-house and held as a controlled record.
Moulding or sheet calendering — shaped gaskets compression moulded; flat gaskets cured as sheet to the specified thickness.
Die-cutting or trimming — flat gaskets cut to the flange profile and bolt pattern; moulded gaskets flash-trimmed.
Quality inspection — dimensional check against the flange standard, hardness testing and batch sampling. Bolt-hole pitch is what is checked.
Export packaging — industrial packing with documentation. ISPM-15 treated pallets where timber packaging is used. Flat gaskets are packed flat and interleaved, never stacked under load.
fields.note:
Six steps, six kept — three need the die-cutting vocabulary. A flange gasket is usually cut from cured sheet, not moulded, and the template describes only the moulded route.
Step 05 is worth the specific: a gasket that is dimensionally perfect but has its bolt holes on the wrong pitch circle is scrap, and it is the check a gasket buyer cares about

notes: The process block must render from the part record.
“Die-cut” and “bolt-hole pitch” are gasket-buyer vocabulary and neither is on this site.
Numbered steps are an <ol>.
